message.content:
Here’s a quick mix of classic and contemporary horror films across several sub‑genres—so you can pick whatever mood strikes you:

| # | Title | Year | Sub‑Genre | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|---|-------|------|-----------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **Psycho** | 1960 | Psychological Thriller | Hitchcock’s masterclass in suspense; the shower scene is legendary. |
| 2 | **The Shining** | 1980 | Supernatural / Psychological | Kubrick’s eerie adaptation of Stephen King; haunting visuals & Jack Nicholson’s iconic performance. |
| 3 | **Halloween** | 1978 | Slasher | The original “killer mask” film that defined the slasher formula; Michael Myers’ silent menace is chilling. |
| 4 | **The Exorcist** | 1973 | Demonic Possession | One of the most unsettling films ever made; its sound design and practical effects still terrify audiences. |
| 5 | **Get Out** | 2017 | Horror‑Comedy / Social Commentary | Jordan Peele blends scares with sharp satire; it’s both funny and deeply unsettling. |
| 6 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | Family Drama / Gothic Horror | A slow‑burn dread that culminates in a truly shocking climax; Toni Collette delivers a tour‑de‑force performance. |
| 7 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Survival / Sci‑Fi Horror | Silence is the main weapon; the tension is palpable and the stakes feel real. |
| 8 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | Folk Horror | Daylight doesn’t always mean safety; the film’s bright setting makes the horror feel even more surreal. |
| 9 | **It Follows** | 2014 | Urban Legend / Psychological | The premise is simple but effective; the soundtrack and pacing keep the dread creeping. |
|10 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | Psychological / Supernatural | A metaphorical look at grief that turns into a genuinely creepy creature feature. |

Feel free to let me know if you’re looking for something specific—like a particular era, sub‑genre, or family‑friendly options—and I can tailor the list further!
